::: {.why}
It reliably improves the shape of a return distribution and much less reliably improves the mean, and knowing which is which stops you from crediting it with the wrong thing.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Decompose the change in Sharpe from volatility targeting into the part from stabilised risk and the part from an implicit timing bet.
- Say what volatility targeting does to maximum drawdown and to the tails, using your own numbers.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Separate the two effects: compare your trend follower targeted with a forecast against the same strategy targeted with a lookahead perfect volatility forecast, and against no targeting. The gap between the first and the second is forecast quality; the gap between the second and the third is the mechanical effect.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Report what actually improved: Sharpe, maximum drawdown, kurtosis of monthly returns, and the volatility of realised volatility, for all three variants. Volatility targeting usually wins on three of those four and only sometimes on the first.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The trend follower now sizes on a volatility forecast from qlib/vol.py rather than on constant notional, and the improvement is decomposed into the mechanical part and the forecast-quality part rather than claimed as a whole.
:::
